verifier_reason: test_outputs.py::test_jump_analyzer_test_video: The test failed in the call phase due to an assertion error

items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Most names are clear (ground_y, elevation_threshold, jump_block), but business logic uses single-letter names (`x, y, w, h`, `w1/w2`, `d`, `f`, `c`). There is no docstring, and the block-grouping and landing-search logic has no comments.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: `analyze_jump` is about 145 lines and does capture, motion diff, background subtraction, tracking, thresholding, block grouping and landing search all in one function. It breaks the requested split between the signal function and the takeoff/landing locator. The airborne list comprehension is copy-pasted.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Checks `cap.isOpened()` and raises a ValueError with a message, and nothing is swallowed. But magic constants are everywhere with no rationale: 0.35/0.72, threshold 20/25, area>150, ±80 window, >30, 15/10/8. The redundant `f == curr[-1] + 1 or f <= curr[-1] + 2` adds noise.

items.name: Robust to bad inputs and missing detections
items.name_zh: 异常输入与检测失败的处理
items.evidence: Validates opening and raises clear ValueErrors (uncaught traceback, non-zero exit) when there is no runner or no jump. Thresholds are mostly absolute pixel constants tuned on the example ('elevation_threshold = 15', '±80', area>150); only ground_y is adaptive. The hidden test failed.

items.name: Output contract honoured
items.evidence: Reads `argv[1]` and writes `/app/output.toml` with exactly the two int fields. The frame numbering convention is never stated: it is 0-based (`frame_idx` starts at 0), while the reference is 1-based. With no argument it silently falls back to `/app/example_video.mp4`.
